details:
Hello, I have a severe visual impairment and I believe that a digital version of my real-life glasses would be very useful to others as well as myself. I use a telescope bolted to a lens on my glasses that I can adjust to zoom in to things at different degrees.

Something like the following would be a minimum viable product:

 - A camera that could be locked to a specific point relative to the head

 - A relatively simple and convenient way to adjust the zoom

 - Effectively minimal frame/controls on the camera

 - A means to adjust how large the camera is

 - The camera would include everything: Characters, UI, everything.

 - It wouldn't record or take pictures, just present an enlarged view to the user.

Perhaps a way to adjust the zoom in the pop-up menu when the aid is turned on would let there be minimal controls and a convenient means to adjust it at once, I don't know. The main thing is to avoid having controls that can't be dismissed occluding chunks of the visual field.

Once one gets used to the magnified area being in a spot in front of one's eye, one can just learn to look down it and around it while turning one's head a bit to semiconsciously get the view one needs.  People who use bioptics (similar devices to what I have) have a similar experience.

(See below!)

Really, really nice to have if possible:

 - Whether the camera itself is on or not does not have to persist between sessions, but it would be really, really nice if the zoom and where the camera is locked persists between sessions so people don't have to fiddle with trying to find where it was last time/get used to it again

 - Binocular mode: Two cameras equal in size/shape/aspect/zoom positioned in the visual field. Symmetrically by default, independently at need. This matches the bioptic configuration that a lot of people have. I don't have stereoscopy so a monocular is fine for me and two cameras would be distracting, but only having one would cause many people vertigo.

 - Letting people adjust width/color of frame (e.g. a white/light colored frame would be very difficult and uncomfortable for me to use, and even many things that might be considered 'dark grey' would be uncomfortably light for me. Black/none should be available.  Similarly, someone else might need a 'bright' frame to clearly separate the two.)

Somewhat nice to have if convenient:

 - Toggle between square and circle

 - Completely frameless (just a floating area of magnification)
title: Magnifying Visual Aid (Accessibility)
